transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-20
Start: 15:30 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Lena (Emerald Head of ML), Marcus (Emerald Infra), Priya (Emerald CISO)
Links shared: deck: https://redwood.app/decks/dedicated-capacity, sizing spreadsheet: https://redwood.app/drive/dedicated-sizing-spreadsheet, soc2 checklist (customer) noted

Summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Emerald Capital is evaluating Dedicated reserved GPU capacity for a production recommender/chat assistant workload. Primary drivers: data isolation, predictable throughput for market hours, and lower per-token costs vs hosted API. Concerns: burst traffic handling, autoscaling latency, encryption/KMS and audit logs, compliance (SOC2) and SSO integration. Agreed next steps: send sizing + pricing, plan a technical deep dive + benchmark window.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh I think we have about 45 minutes. I'm Samir, account exec for Redwood. With me is Maya our solutions engineer. How's it going?
[00:07] Lena: Hi Samir, thanks. I'm Lena (Head of ML) at Emerald. Marcus and Priya are on too. We've been looking at dedicated for about a month.
[00:12] Marcus: Hey all. Quick note, hope audio's ok.
[00:15] Maya: Good, thanks. Quick agenda, if that's ok: we want to cover current infra/requirements, suggested Dedicated sizing and how burst works, security/compliance checklist, and then next steps. Sound good?
[00:27] Lena: Yep. We'll also talk about cost targets — we have a cost-per-1k tokens baseline from our hosted experiments.
[00:33] Samir: Perfect. Marcus, can you give a quick overview of the stack and traffic patterns?
[00:37] Marcus: Sure. So we're running models for a customer support assistant and a personalization ranking pipeline. Peak real-time latency sensitive traffic is 300 qps across a fleet during market hours, p95 latency target 150ms for short-turn chat flows. Background jobs are batch re-ranks and embeddings. Right now we run on a mix of internal infra and a hosted LLM provider but cost and data isolation are pushing us to explore Dedicated. Important: we need network isolation and VPC peering, and keys in our KMS/H S M - sorry HSM — we want HSM-backed keys.
[01:10] Priya: From security side, SOC2 and data residency in US only. Also need audit logs and RBAC integration with our SAML S S O.
[01:18] Samir: Understood. Maya, do you want to take sizing?
[01:20] Maya: Yeah, quick note: when we say Dedicated we mean reserved GPU pools that are isolated to your account — predictable throughput and no noisy neighbor. For the 300 qps figure, a starting point could be four A100-ish equivalents for the real-time model, depending on model family and sequence length. That gets you headroom and allows for burst capacity patterns with our burst pool add-on. But there are a couple of variables: model size, quantization, sequence length distribution, and KV cache hit rates.
[01:46] Lena: We're using a 7B-ish open model for chat right now and are testing 13B for ranking. Sequence lengths average 128 tokens for chat, 64 for ranking.
[01:56] Maya: Ok so 7B for chat is fairly cheap on tokens; if you tune batching and prefix KV caching you'll reduce compute significantly. For 300 qps with p95 150ms that's tight — we may need more GPUs or lower latency variants. Also our runtime can do continuous batching and low-latency kernels, but there's a tradeoff.
[02:14] Marcus: How does burst capacity work? We have spikes during product launches where qps briefly doubles for 20-30 minutes. We don't want to pay for steady-state that covers very short spikes.
[02:23] Samir: Good question. Maya?
[02:25] Maya: We have a burst model: dedicated has a reserved baseline and a burst pool customers on the same region can tap into — it routes by policy and capacity availability. Burst is not guaranteed like reserved, but it's designed for short bursts. For strict guarantees you'd size reserved to cover your SLOs; for cost efficiency you pick reserved for 70–80% of expected peak and rely on burst for the rest. We can also configure autoscaling policies that pre-warm extra nodes on schedule, e.g., pre-scale 10 minutes before market open.
[02:53] Lena: That pre-warm idea sounds helpful — we can predict traffic spikes. What about scaling latency? If autoscaler adds nodes, how long until they're ready?
[03:03] Maya: Typical cold scale can be 2–6 minutes depending on model size and how much we need to warm caches; warm pool pre-provisioning reduces that to under a minute. Note there's also KV cache population time; we can seed caches during warm-up using representative prefix sets.
[03:18] Marcus: And network isolation, VPC options? We need private deployment or at least VPC peering.
[03:23] Samir: For Dedicated we offer VPC peering and private networking to the customer's VPC; for strictest cases we also do Private deployment (customer-managed control plane). Which are you leaning to?
[03:31] Priya: Prefer Dedicated with VPC peering initially; Private might be an option later if compliance requires on-prem. Also need KMS integration and customer-managed keys.
[03:39] Maya: We integrate with major KMS providers and HSM-backed keys. Audit logs are exportable to your SIEM and we offer fine-grained RBAC, SAML SSO for user auth. Small caveat: encryption at rest for model artifacts vs payload logs — we can ensure payloads are not persisted by default but we can also configure retention policies.
[03:59] Lena: How deterministic is quality when you quantize models? We want to use 4-bit quant to save costs but need to ensure no regression on our ranking MRR.
[04:07] Maya: This is where Redwood Optimize helps — we run automated evals on your prompt sets and recommend quantization profiles. We can run quality gates and rollback if we detect a regression. Suggest we run an A/B test in the benchmark window.
[04:20] Lena: That sounds good. On SLA — we need at least 99.9% during market hours. Can you get that in Dedicated?
[04:27] Samir: Yes, our Dedicated SLA can be tailored (networking caveats apply). We'll include SLA language in the contract and service levels for uptime and latency. We'll surface the details in the pricing doc.
[04:36] Marcus: One more infra question: how do you handle KV cache across nodes? If we scale horizontally, is cache sharded or global?
[04:43] Maya: RT, the KV cache is node-local but we have a prefix cache layer that syncs warmed prefixes to nodes. In practice for low-latency chat we recommend sticky routing or sticky sessions to keep the KV close, and pre-warming ensures cache hits. There's some mis-transcription sometimes where folks call it K V cache and we say yeah.
[04:58] Lena: (laughs) noted.
[05:01] Priya: Compliance — how do you handle audit logs and access reviews? We need tamper-evident logs and quarterly access reviews.
[05:08] Maya: Logs are exported to your SIEM, we can sign and time-stamp audit events; we also provide access reports. For quarterly access review we can provide an admin CSV dump. We'll include SOC2 artifacts and our contact for compliance review.
[05:21] Samir: We'll include our SOC2 report and standard questionnaire. Priya, would you like to run an initial security technical review with our security engineer?
[05:27] Priya: Yes, please. Schedule that.
[05:30] Samir: Great.
[05:32] Maya: Back to cost — to help you estimate cost-per-call, we'll run a 2-week benchmark on Dedicated reserved pool. We'll need a sample traffic trace and prompt set. We can also mirror production traffic if you want.
[05:44] Lena: We can share a 24-hour sample trace and the prompt set. We'll sanitize PII.
[05:49] Samir: Perfect. We'll use that to size the pool and propose pricing.
[05:52] Marcus: On billing — is there per-GPU hourly billing for burst or is it per-token for bursted capacity?
[05:58] Maya: Reserved is a committed monthly price (or annual). Burst is billed on usage — typically a per-minute GPU equivalent rate plus token charges depending on the model. We'll send the exact billing matrix; it's in the sizing spreadsheet.
[06:09] Lena: Anything about multi-region? Low-latency users on east and west coast.
[06:13] Maya: We can deploy dedicated pools per region and have routing policies. If you need cross-region failover we can replicate model artifacts to the secondary region. There's additional storage and replication cost.
[06:24] Priya: Data residency: must remain in US.
[06:27] Samir: Noted — we'll ensure region constraints.
[06:29] Maya: One caveat on burst — because it's shared across a region, heavy usage in the region could reduce burst availability; we recommend a small committed burst buffer for critical launch windows or scheduled pre-warm.
[06:41] Lena: For benchmarks, can we test both hosted API and Dedicated to compare latency/cost?
[06:46] Maya: Absolutely, we'll run side-by-side tests and a quality/regression eval. Our Optimize tooling will surface per-request cost and p95/p50 latency breakdowns so you can compare.
[06:56] Marcus: How does rollback work if a model version causes regressions?
[06:59] Maya: We support pinned model versions and can do canary rollouts with automatic fallback. You can define health checks and quality thresholds; if thresholds fail we auto-fallback to previous stable model.
[07:09] Lena: Good.
[07:10] Samir: Any other blockers?
[07:12] Priya: Need to see SOC2 and network architecture. Also want to confirm we can use our HSM provider for keys.
[07:18] Maya: Yes to HSM and we'll share architecture diagrams.
[07:21] Samir: Ok recap: we'll send pricing + sizing spreadsheet, schedule a 2-hour technical deep dive with Marcus and infra, provision a 2-week benchmark window (trial Dedicated pool), and Maya will draft benchmark plan. Priya will provide SOC2 scope and compliance checklist.
[07:36] Lena: Timeline: we'd like to start the benchmark in first week of Nov. Is that feasible?
[07:41] Samir: Yes, with paperwork and approvals we can aim for that.
[07:44] Marcus: One last thing, on the model side we may switch to a 13B ranker in prod; can you support mixed model families in the same pool or do we need separate pools?
[07:54] Maya: You can run mixed families but performance isolation is better with separate pools if the 13B has very different memory/throughput. We can also run routing policies to send heavier workloads to dedicated 13B nodes and keep chat on 7B nodes.
[08:08] Lena: Ok that makes sense.
[08:10] Samir: Great — any closing comments?
[08:12] Priya: No, thanks. Please send SOC2 and schedule the security review.
[08:17] Samir: Will do. Thanks everyone.
[08:20] [call ends]
